Q6_check_content_access_retention.decision: DIVERGE from conformance section F5. PR-07 retains all 30 check_content_access call sites instead of substituting them for Viewer.
Q6_check_content_access_retention.rationale: Migration 062 adds `visibility varchar(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'public'` to every tier_a table and backfills nothing. No PR before PR-12 transcribes ownership.partition_type into claims.visibility. So TODAY every spliced viewer predicate matches every row, and check_content_access is the only control with live effect on the handlers that have one. Deleting the sites now would take a fixture-private claim from redacted to fully readable by a stranger's token - the removal, not the retention, would be the fail-open. Two filters compose strictly narrower than either.

followup_2026_09_02.note: An adversarial review of the first pass raised 17 findings, 10 of them blocker/major. ALL TEN WERE FIXED - none was rejected. This block records what each was and how it was closed, because the previous pass's failure mode was committing with known fail-opens unfixed.

The same Viewer-held-but-never-spent shape as frame_claims_sorted, and hypothesis.rs contains ZERO check_content_access calls, so the register's stated compensating control did not exist here. Now ClaimRepository::content_and_properties (spliced). ClaimRow deleted. Guarded by hypothesis_status_http_hides_a_group_private_claim_from_a_stranger, which asserts 404-for-a-stranger with a public-claim non-vacuity control.
followup_2026_09_02.B2_register_justification_false: FIXED. The register's claim that 'the compensating control is the per-row check_content_access pass, which PR-14 deletes - that is the deadline' was false for most entries. Only claims.rs and edges.rs contain check_content_access at all. The register is now split into COMPENSATED_INLINE_READS (claims.rs, edges.rs) and UNCOMPENSATED_INLINE_READS (nine files), with the deadline restated as PR-12 for the uncompensated set, and the doc now explicitly declines to assert that the compensating call sits on the return path of the specific counted statement - which is the over-claim that produced the original error.

followup_2026_09_02.M4_semantic_probe_siblings: FIXED. PR-07's headline find - a caller-supplied probe vector ranked against the whole corpus returning content, unfiltered - was fixed in search.rs and rag.rs and left standing in FOUR siblings: voids.rs::detect_voids, voids.rs::embedding_density (two sites), gaps.rs::gap_analysis and experiments.rs::hypothesize. A FIFTH site the finding did not name was fixed too: hypothesize's clustering branch pulled raw embedding::real[] vectors for the 200 nearest claims, and PR-07's own acceptance criteria treat a raw embedding as approximately invertible to content.
followup_2026_09_02.M5_belief_at_time_evidence: FIXED. computation.rs::belief_at_time held a Viewer, spent it on ClaimRepository::get_by_id, and then read the evidence it replays with an inline unfiltered statement. evidence and edges are BOTH tier_a, so both were filterable and neither was filtered. Now EvidenceRepository::provided_for_claim_as_of with /* {VISIBILITY:e} */ and /* {VISIBILITY:ed} */ (the edges marker in the JOIN's ON clause, matching count_all_evidence_for_claim). The test seeds one group-private evidence row AND one public evidence row behind a group-private edge, so deleting EITHER marker turns it red.
followup_2026_09_02.M7_visibility_lint_missing: FIXED. crates/epigraph-db/tests/visibility_lint.rs did not exist, despite being cited three times in visibility.rs, seven times in repos/lineage.rs, twice in repos/claim.rs and once in FINAL-PLAN.md as PR-06's gate - the same cited-but-unwritten defect PR-07's own commit message indicts. It now exists: every fn under src/repos/ taking a &Viewer and running SQL must call .splice(, carry the literal static predicate `visibility = 'public'`, or carry a VISIBILITY-EXEMPT: marker. 193 viewer-taking fns scanned, 0 violations. NOTE: group_bind()/bypass_bind() are deliberately NOT accepted as evidence of spending - binding an array proves a parameter was supplied, not that the SQL reads it, and a frame_claims_sorted-shaped fail-open would pass a lint keyed on the accessor. Falsified under mutation: stripping viewer.splice from ChallengeRepository::list_for_claim makes it fail, naming challenge.rs:88.
followup_2026_09_02.M8_subgraph_edges_false_doc: FIXED. subgraph_edges' doc asserted 'the caller additionally narrows node_ids to the ids that survived the node projections'. No caller did: load_subgraph fetched edges FIRST, before any node projection ran. Because edges.visibility defaults to 'public', the response's edges array enumerated claim ids the nodes projection had withheld - the id-enumeration oracle PR-07 says it closed in graph_neighborhood.rs. load_subgraph now runs the four node projections first and passes the surviving ids; the doc states the obligation as a precondition instead of asserting a property it cannot enforce. Falsified under mutation: restoring the raw node_ids call makes load_subgraph_never_returns_an_edge_naming_a_withheld_node fail with the exact edge id.
followup_2026_09_02.M9_reasoning_traces_wrong_justification: FIXED. load_subgraph's doc left reasoning_traces unfiltered on the stated grounds that it 'is NOT in tier_a ... has no owner_group_id to filter on'. It IS in migration 062's tier_a array, beside challenges and experiment_triples, and does carry the tenancy columns. The disclosure was small (a methodology label and a confidence float); the wrong justification was the defect, because the next reader re-derives 'nothing to filter' from it and never revisits the site. Now filtered through GraphViewRepository::subgraph_traces. The `agents` half of the same sentence was re-checked and is correct - agents genuinely is not tier_a.

open_findings.what: RESOLVED-ON-BRANCH. The not(db) parity shim is now both CI-gated and executed locally.
open_findings.detail: The previous entry said 'the prescribed gate never compiles this configuration' while bearer.rs's own doc and public_router_allowlist.rs's header both asserted that .github/workflows/ci.yml gates `cargo check -p epigraph-api --no-default-features --locked`. The ledger and the code were asserting opposite things. The code is right: ci.yml line 171 runs exactly that step, deliberately scoped lib+bins rather than --all-targets because epigraph-api's [dev-dependencies] on epigraph-db and sqlx are non-optional. It has also now been executed locally in a SEPARATE target dir (/home/jeremy/.cargo-target-nodb) - a warm shared dir holding default-feature artifacts returns exit 0 on a tree that fails cold, which produced a false green twice on this project.

open_findings.what: Aggregate and existence oracles run unfiltered in handlers that are already holding a Viewer
open_findings.detail: `SELECT COUNT(*), AVG(conflict_k), MAX(conflict_k) FROM mass_functions WHERE frame_id = $1`; `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM claims WHERE id = $1)` deciding 404-vs-200; two `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edges ... relationship = 'decomposes_to'` deciding center_kind. mass_functions, claims and edges are all tier_a, so all three are filterable and the fix is a parameter rather than a redesign. These disclose existence and cardinality, never text. NOT FIXED IN PR-07: they are outside the inline-content-read class the lint polices and outside this PR's charter, and bundling them would have made the diff harder to review than the leaks it is about. Raised by the adversarial review as minor.

open_findings.what: Write-path authorization reads run unfiltered while the handler holds a Viewer
open_findings.detail: `SELECT agent_id FROM claims WHERE id = $1` is the ownership check the supersede decision rests on; `SELECT id FROM claims WHERE id = $1 AND 'workflow' = ANY(labels)` is deprecate_workflow's only existence gate. They let a principal act on a claim it cannot read. Consistent with the deliberate PR-16 deferral documented in repos/evidence.rs::delete, but unlike the repo-layer deferrals these carry no such comment at the site and no ratchet tracks them.

open_findings.what: The fail-open ratchet counts ONE literal spelling of the idiom, so a variant spelling raises no error
open_findings.detail: The needle is `if let Some(axum::Extension(ref auth)) = auth_ctx`. agents.rs::create_agent uses the same idiom in two forms the needle misses: `= &auth_ctx` (trailing &) and `Some(axum::Extension(auth))` (no ref). The ratchet is therefore monotone only against one transcription. Separately, the register's rationale ('harmless only because a ViewerExtractor earlier in the same signature 401s first') does not hold for create_agent, which has no ViewerExtractor and no other auth extractor - nothing in that handler 401s and the agents:write scope is simply unchecked when AuthContext is absent. NOT FIXED IN PR-07: re-baselining that ratchet in the same PR that re-baselines the content-read register would have meant two simultaneous redefinitions, and the second would have hidden the first.
open_findings.assigned: PR-16, which owns the write-path fail-opens the ratchet tracks

open_findings.what: atom_count is derived from an `atoms` CTE filtered only on claim_neighborhood_membership, not on claims
open_findings.detail: The CTE carries /* {VISIBILITY:m} */ only; the returned atom_count therefore tells a stranger how many atoms a compound decomposes into, including atoms whose claims rows it cannot read. No invisible content escapes - the final SELECT filters the compound's own claims row. Inert today because claim_neighborhood_membership.visibility defaults to 'public'. Reportable because MassFunctionRepository::count_for_claim's doc, added by this same PR, spends a paragraph forbidding exactly this shape ('a bare COUNT(*) here would be a cardinality oracle'), and applying that standard in one file and not two files away is an inconsistency worth recording.

open_findings.where: crates/epigraph-api/src/routes/ (97 ViewerExtractor handlers, 62 of which reference `viewer` exactly once)
open_findings.what: No mechanical check distinguishes a handler that spends its Viewer on the content read from one that spends it on an unrelated scalar
open_findings.detail: All 97 handlers reference `viewer` at least once, so there are no literally-unused Viewers; the live defect class is SINGLE-SPEND. Both hypothesis_status (B1) and belief_at_time (M5) were single-spend handlers, and both were found by opening the file rather than by any scan. The adversarial review hand-read roughly a dozen of the 62; the remaining ~50 are unreviewed by any mechanism. The widened viewer_route_table_lint now catches the subset whose second read is an inline tier_a projection - which is what caught the belief_at_time shape - but a handler whose leak is in a repo function it calls with the wrong argument is still invisible.

open_findings.what: No test asserts that a scoped caller's server-derived theme centroid excludes claims it cannot see
open_findings.detail: The statement carries /* {VISIBILITY:c} */ on the averaged SELECT, so the predicate is present and visibility_lint.rs now enforces that it stays. But create_theme_with_centroid_averages_the_claims_when_no_centroid_is_sent uses a claims:admin token over an all-public fixture, so the tenancy half is unasserted. See the crud.rs_create_theme_with_centroid entry in PR-07's scope_substitution.
open_findings.assigned: PR-12 or PR-16, whichever first makes a non-admin caller reach this path
